title: FEMA disaster assistance for individuals: information and documents
use_when: Use when a household is applying to FEMA for Individual Assistance after a declared disaster, or must prove occupancy or ownership afterward; for SBA disaster home loans also use sba-disaster-loan-home, and for an NFIP flood claim use insurance-nfip-flood-claim.
note: Built from the DisasterAssistance.gov Disaster Survivor Application Checklist (last updated 04/20/2026) and FEMA's page on verifying home ownership or occupancy (last updated June 26, 2026). It does not decide eligibility or award amounts, and documents FEMA asks for in a specific letter or for a specific disaster may differ.

da-checklist.name: DisasterAssistance.gov, Disaster Survivor Application Checklist (Last Updated: 04/20/2026)

fema-verify.name: FEMA, Verifying Home Ownership or Occupancy (page last updated June 26, 2026)

situations.direct-deposit: Does the household want any award paid by direct deposit?
situations.occupancy-check: Has FEMA asked the household to prove it lived in the damaged home?
situations.ownership-check: Has FEMA asked the household to prove it owns the damaged home?
situations.no-documents: Does the household have none of the listed occupancy or ownership documents, and does it live in a mobile home, travel trailer, insular area, island or tribal land, or an inherited home?

items.label: Social Security number of the applicant, another adult, or a minor child in the household
items.detail: Application checklist: that person must also be a U.S. citizen, non-citizen national, or qualified alien. Anyone without a number is sent to the Social Security Number and Card page first. Send through the secure portal, never by plain email.

items.label: Types of insurance coverage the household has (homeowners, flood, auto, mobile home)
Description of the damage, the type of disaster, and the type of home or vehicle
items.detail: For example flood, hurricane or earthquake; condo, mobile home or house; car or truck.

items.label: Total annual household income before taxes at the time of the disaster
Address of the damaged property, plus a current address, phone number and email
Bank name, account type, routing number and account number
items.detail: Optional, for direct deposit. Send through the secure portal, never by plain email.

items.label: One document showing the household lived at the damaged home
items.detail: Any one of: lease, housing agreement or rent receipts; utility bill; employer statement such as a pay stub; bank or credit card statement; motor vehicle registration; affidavit of residency or other court document; document from a public official, medical provider or social service organization; local school documents showing the child's damaged address and the applicant's or co-applicant's name; a post-disaster letter from the mobile home park owner or manager confirming occupancy. Most documents should be dated within 1 year before the disaster and/or within the 18-month period of assistance. Send through the secure portal, never by plain email.

items.label: Driver's license, state ID or voter registration card showing the damaged address
items.detail: Accepted as the one occupancy document. Must be dated before the disaster and not expired when sent to FEMA. Send through the secure portal, never by plain email.

items.label: One document showing the household owns the damaged home
items.detail: Any one of: deed or official record; mortgage documents; homeowners insurance documents; property tax receipt or bill; manufactured home certificate or title; home purchase contract such as a bill of sale or land installment contract; a will, or an heirship affidavit with the death certificate, naming the applicant as heir; receipts for major repairs or maintenance dated within 5 years before the disaster; court documents; a post-disaster letter from the mobile home park owner or manager, or a public official. Most documents should be dated within 1 year before the disaster and/or within the 18-month period of assistance. Send through the secure portal, never by plain email.

items.label: Signed self-declarative statement, as a last resort
items.detail: Must include the address, how long it was the primary residence, the applicant's name and signature, a good-faith-effort declaration, why documents could not be obtained, and a penalty-of-perjury declaration in FEMA's wording. For heirship, also the decedent's death certificate and a statement that the applicant is the nearest relative in the line of succession.
